title: Graduate Gaming Hardware and Research Thesis
purpose: Evaluate advanced architectures, physical design and verification, then complete and defend a research artifact.

modules.title: Advanced computer architecture for gaming workloads
modules.project: Perform an architecture study using a pinned simulator or a carefully bounded analytical model. Compare at least three configurations on representative and adverse game-related workloads, and validate the model against a known reference where possible.

lessons.title: Cache coherence, memory consistency and synchronization
lessons.outcome: Separate agreement about a location from ordering across locations.
lessons.practical_assignment: Model a small coherence protocol and evaluate message-passing litmus tests under stated language and hardware models. Pass: ownership invariants hold, transient races are considered and coherence is not confused with data-race freedom.
lessons.assigned_reading: R48: multiprocessors, coherence and consistency; R35: selected memory-ordering specification; R11: language-level concurrency.

lessons.title: Out-of-order execution, speculation and precise state
lessons.outcome: Increase instruction overlap without changing architectural outcomes.
lessons.practical_assignment: Use a simulator or detailed scheduling model to compare in-order and out-of-order execution on independent and dependent instruction streams. Pass: architectural results agree and bottleneck explanations include true dependencies and resource limits.
lessons.assigned_reading: R48: superscalar, out-of-order, prediction and exception handling; R38: CPU models and configuration.

lessons.title: Architecture simulation, traces and model validation
lessons.outcome: Use simulation as evidence with a stated fidelity boundary.
lessons.practical_assignment: Run a cache, scheduling or accelerator study with at least one validation case and a sensitivity sweep. Pass: raw configurations reproduce results, modeled versus measured quantities are labeled and conclusions do not exceed the tested fidelity.
lessons.assigned_reading: R38: simulation models, statistics and configuration; R48: architecture evaluation; R43: analytical bounds.

lessons.title: Memory systems, chiplets and multi-objective design
lessons.outcome: Choose an architecture across performance, power, cost and complexity.
lessons.practical_assignment: Construct a Pareto comparison of at least three architecture configurations. Pass: objectives and assumptions are explicit, dominated designs are identified correctly and a recommendation changes appropriately when a hard constraint changes.
lessons.assigned_reading: R48: memory and quantitative design; R49: packaging and system tradeoffs; R38: architecture alternatives.

modules.title: VLSI, timing and physical implementation
modules.prerequisites: Modules 31-34, 40 and 46. Use educational libraries and licensed or open tools only.
modules.project: Carry a verified small RTL block through an educational synthesis and physical-design flow. Report constraints, timing, area and power-estimation assumptions. The result is a learning artifact, not fabrication-ready commercial signoff.

lessons.title: CMOS logic, transistor sizing and delay models
lessons.outcome: Connect gate-level choices to electrical load and timing.
lessons.practical_assignment: Analyze and simulate an inverter chain or compare library-cell drive strengths under several loads. Pass: assumptions are stated, input loading is included and model predictions are compared with available characterized or simulated results.
lessons.assigned_reading: R49: CMOS devices, combinational circuits and delay; R30: MOS circuit foundations.

lessons.title: Static timing analysis, clocks and timing exceptions
lessons.outcome: Check every required path under the correct timing contract.
lessons.practical_assignment: Constrain a small sequential block and inspect worst setup and hold paths. Pass: no unexplained unconstrained endpoints, every exception is justified and a deliberately tightened clock produces an understood violation.
lessons.assigned_reading: R39: timing analysis and flow constraints; R49: sequential timing and clocking.

lessons.title: Synthesis, placement, clock trees, routing and physical checks
lessons.outcome: Understand how a logical netlist becomes a physical layout.
lessons.practical_assignment: Run a small block through an educational OpenROAD-compatible flow or inspect a provided open example. Pass: capture stage reports, identify a routing/timing change and state which physical checks were and were not performed.
lessons.assigned_reading: R39: flow stages, placement, clock tree and routing; R49: physical-design methodology and EDA.

lessons.title: Power, area, process corners and design-space closure
lessons.outcome: Report PPA with enough assumptions to make comparison meaningful.
lessons.practical_assignment: Compare two verified RTL implementations using identical flow assumptions. Pass: report area, worst timing and activity-based power estimates where supported, with uncertainty and no unsupported commercial-silicon claim.
lessons.assigned_reading: R49: power, timing and implementation tradeoffs; R39: reports and analysis; R30: energy and electrical models.

modules.title: Verification, reliability and hardware trust boundaries
modules.project: Create a verification dossier for the hardware capstone: requirements-to-tests traceability, assertions, coverage, clock/reset review, fault injection and a clearly bounded assurance claim.

lessons.title: Formal properties, abstraction and assume-guarantee reasoning
lessons.outcome: Prove useful properties without hiding failures in assumptions.
lessons.practical_assignment: Prove a queue, arbiter or transaction property and inject a violation. Pass: assumptions are reviewed independently, contention is covered and bounded, proven, failed and unknown results are reported separately.
lessons.assigned_reading: R50: safety, liveness, induction, cover and assumptions; R49: verification methodology.

lessons.title: Clock/reset crossings and asynchronous FIFO verification
lessons.outcome: Check digital protocol correctness while acknowledging analog risk.
lessons.practical_assignment: Model an asynchronous FIFO or event handshake with independent clocks and reset sequences. Pass: no loss/duplication under the stated protocol, full/empty behavior is checked and physical synchronizer assumptions are listed separately.
lessons.assigned_reading: R50: multiclock modeling and verification; R49: sequential circuits and synchronization; revisit Module 32 timing boundaries.

lessons.title: Fault models, ECC, testability and recovery
lessons.outcome: Design for detectable failures rather than assuming perfect hardware.
lessons.practical_assignment: Implement a parity and a small single-error-correcting code model, then inject faults. Pass: enumerate the supported correction/detection claims, test multi-bit counterexamples and define a recovery response.
lessons.assigned_reading: R49: testing, DFT and reliability context; R51: error detection/correction reporting concepts; R06: coding and combinatorial reasoning extension.

lessons.title: Hardware security, thermal limits and assurance review
lessons.outcome: Include isolation and failure containment in the design contract.
lessons.practical_assignment: Write a threat-and-failure review for the accelerator and test malformed descriptors, denied access and reset under load in simulation. Pass: isolation limits, protection assumptions and unresolved risks are explicit; no unauthorized target testing occurs.
lessons.assigned_reading: R51: device access, DMA and isolation; R49: implementation and verification; R50: enforceable protocol properties.

modules.title: Master's thesis: proposal, implementation and evaluation
modules.prerequisites: Gate I and relevant advanced-track modules; independent technical mentorship strongly recommended.
modules.project: Prepare and execute a thesis-scale project in one primary specialization. Budget 400-800 focused hours as a planning range, with scope adjusted through review. The deliverable is a defensible contribution and reproducible artifact, not a promise of publication.

lessons.title: Question selection, literature map and thesis scope
lessons.outcome: Turn a broad interest into a falsifiable, feasible research question.
lessons.practical_assignment: Write a 3-5 page proposal with a research question, 8-15 relevant sources, baseline plan, constraints and exclusions. Pass: a reviewer can explain what observation would weaken or refute the main hypothesis.
lessons.assigned_reading: Use Module 41's paper method and the chosen track's original papers; R44, R48, R49 or R55 are starting anchors, not a substitute for the literature search.

lessons.title: Proposal review, baselines and risk-reduction milestones
lessons.outcome: Make failure cheap before the expensive implementation phase.
lessons.practical_assignment: Deliver a running baseline, risk register and milestone plan. Pass: the primary metric can be measured, a small feasibility experiment exists and each major risk has a mitigation or explicit acceptance decision.
lessons.assigned_reading: R49: project milestone and reporting structure; Module 41: experimental design; chosen method's primary documentation.

lessons.title: Implementation, ablations and controlled evaluation
lessons.outcome: Execute the study without changing the question to fit a favorable result.
lessons.practical_assignment: Run the approved evaluation with baselines, at least one ablation and one sensitivity study. Pass: scripts regenerate results, failed cases remain visible and claims use the preregistered primary metric or clearly disclose deviations.
lessons.assigned_reading: R09 and Module 41: uncertainty; chosen track's original methods and implementation references; handbook experiment manifest.

lessons.title: Thesis writing, reproducibility and contribution boundaries
lessons.outcome: Write a technical argument another engineer can audit.
lessons.practical_assignment: Produce a thesis-style report, typically 30-60 pages plus appendices as a planning guide, and a complete artifact package. Pass: a reviewer traces five major claims to evidence and reproduces the central table or experiment.
lessons.assigned_reading: R49: final project reports; chosen original papers for reporting comparisons; handbook thesis outline and evidence checklist.

modules.title: Thesis defense, professional practice and continued development
modules.prerequisites: Module 49 and all prerequisites for the selected specialization.
modules.project: Gate J: defend the thesis, pass an independent artifact reproduction, complete a maintainable handoff and publish an honest portfolio where rights permit. This completes the self-study program, not an accredited degree.

lessons.title: Oral defense and independent artifact reproduction
lessons.outcome: Show that the learner owns the reasoning and implementation.
lessons.practical_assignment: Hold a 30-45 minute technical defense with a qualified reviewer or peer panel and a separate artifact run. Pass: the central result is reproduced, major questions receive evidence-based answers and required revisions are completed.
lessons.assigned_reading: R49: design-project evaluation as a reference; handbook defense questions and rubric.

lessons.title: Mature-codebase integration, review and maintainable contributions
lessons.outcome: Transfer a prototype into an engineering environment with other owners.
lessons.practical_assignment: Integrate one tested improvement into a mature open codebase or a maintained local fork. Pass: a focused patch, regression test, design rationale and reviewer response are included, whether or not an upstream project accepts it.
lessons.assigned_reading: R05: distributed workflows and contributing; R11: interfaces and maintenance; R26: mature-engine comparison where authorized.

lessons.title: Portfolio, technical interviews and role-specific evidence
lessons.outcome: Present concrete engineering competence without inflated claims.
lessons.practical_assignment: Prepare three portfolio case studies and complete one systems, one algorithm and one specialization mock interview. Pass: every claimed result is supported by an artifact and assistance or third-party contributions are clearly attributed.
lessons.assigned_reading: R01-R02: breadth review; R11: engineering explanation and contracts; handbook role map and portfolio template.

lessons.title: Long-term learning, maintenance and final handoff
lessons.outcome: Keep the knowledge and artifacts useful after the course ends.
lessons.practical_assignment: Complete Gate J: archive the thesis artifact, produce a maintainer handoff and write a 90-day learning plan with one primary gap and one real contribution goal. Pass: another person can locate, build and understand the project without the author's machine.
lessons.assigned_reading: R05: maintenance workflows; R01-R02: periodic breadth review; current official documentation for the selected tools when an update is undertaken.
